quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well in advance. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to retaliate.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and put distance between yourself and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If a car hits you from behind, this prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When turning, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: Into the first available legal lane.
Into the lane farthest from your direction of travel.
Into any lane.
Into the second-closest available lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Into the first available legal lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the first available legal lane. This is the safest method because you cross fewer lanes and avoid collisions.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop immediately and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They indicate that work is being done on or next to the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, affects your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and lowers your inhibitions, making you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws?

options.text: They are right because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill road is ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency stops. Emergency stops can cause the car behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before you cross. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or sirens approaches, pull to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, yield to other traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
You are entering a reduced speed zone.
You may see more pedestrians.
You are leaving a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are leaving a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: An "End school zone" sign marks the end of a reduced speed zone. You can now drive at normal speeds.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a flagger directs you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights or gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You can stop long enough to unload packages.
You can stop to avoid hitting other vehicles.
You can stop to let out passengers.
You can stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop to avoid hitting other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if cars are approaching.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on crossing roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop and yield to vehicles and pedestrians. Go again when it is safe.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Use your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed yellow line means you can pass the vehicle ahead when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs along with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces the effects of alcohol on your driving.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal drugs, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter medicines) can harm your brain function and your ability to drive safely. Mixing alcohol with any drug greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can enter the intersection in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: If you see this sign, what must you do?

options.text: Do not pass another vehicle.
You can pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You can pass if you know the road ahead.
You can pass, but only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. You must follow the rules shown on regulatory signs. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in this area.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle while staying in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcycles the full width of a lane. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle rider needs space to turn safely.

questions.question: After you stop for a school bus unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you before going.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After you stop for a school bus with its lights flashing and stop arm out, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:

options.text: Illegal.
Smart.
Safe.
Optional.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. It blocks drivers behind you and causes them to switch lanes unsafely. Under normal driving conditions, driving far below the speed limit is against the law.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across lanes to make a turn.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as if they were calm.
Can drive faster because their senses are sharper.
Should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, crying, or depression make it hard to drive safely. These feelings distract you from the road. Calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Shallow water is more dangerous than deep water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on a wet road, your tires cannot push water away as well. If you go fast enough, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane (slide on a layer of water).

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with a siren and/or flashing lights approaches you, what must you do immediately?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, you must drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Under no conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and be careful.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down more quickly.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, your reactions slow down. You feel more confident but make more driving mistakes.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you see it. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When may you go through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check that there is no cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Follow closer to other cars.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, avoid sudden changes in speed or direction. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from crossing guards, signs, and law enforcement in school zones. Drive with extra care in these areas.
